subject: DPA annex: network egress mapping + CMK operator responsibilities
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: legal@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA annex: network egress mapping + CMK operator responsibilities

Hi Brett / Acme Legal team,

Following our call last week, attaching a first-pass annex to the DPA that focuses on two items you asked about: (1) a network egress/dataflow map we maintain for private deployments (VPC & on-prem) and (2) explicit responsibilities around customer-managed keys (CMK) and operator access.

Key asks from your side were: a clear list of subprocessors that might touch telemetry, exact egress paths for telemetry vs. customer payload, and an operational statement about Redwood operators' ability (or inability) to access keys tied to a private deploy. The attached spreadsheet is an egress mapping sample — it shows control-plane callouts, optional telemetry sinks, and export controls.

Please review the attached DPA annex (DPA_Annex_CMK_Operator_Responsibilities_v1.pdf) and the egress map. If you can send redlines or a prioritized list of open items by Wednesday we can prepare a tracked-changes version and an implementation timeline.

Proposed timeline:
- You send redlines by 2026-05-06 EOD
- Redwood provides response + updated annex by 2026-05-07

Thanks — want to keep this tight so we can close procurement next week.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]

Attachments: DPA_Annex_CMK_Operator_Responsibilities_v1.pdf, acme-egress-map-20260504.xlsx

From: Brett Simmons <brett.simmons@acmehealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA annex: network egress mapping + CMK operator responsibilities

Jordan,

Thanks for the docs. A few high-level items from Legal & Procurement after a quick pass:

1) Redlines to the CMK section — our preferred language is that customer retains sole key custodianship and that Redwood is explicitly prohibited from exporting or escrow-rotating customer CMKs without express documented authorization. We attached our suggested redlines (redlines-acme-dpa-20260505.docx).

2) Subprocessor list — can you provide a committed subprocessor roster for private deployments? We need a static list for the DPA annex and a 30-day notice window for any changes.

3) Network egress map — the spreadsheet is helpful but we need a clarified column that separates payload egress (customer data) vs. telemetry/metrics (anonymized). Also specify which telemetry is optional and how to opt out.

4) Operator breakglass — we require an operator breakglass playbook with logs and 3rd-party attestation in the event of forensic access. Please confirm Redwood's proposed attestation cadence.

We are constrained to close this week. If you can incorporate these items and provide a marked-up annex, procurement can take it to signature.

-Brett
Brett Simmons
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Acme Health
brett.simmons@acmehealth.com

Attachments: redlines-acme-dpa-20260505.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: DPA annex: network egress mapping + CMK operator responsibilities

Kimberly / Irene — forwarding Brett's redlines and asks. Quick notes:

- CMK language: Acme wants explicit prohibition on Redwood exporting/escrowing CMKs without express authorization. We already offer a BYOK model for private deploys where keys never leave customer KMS, but we need to be explicit about operator actions (rotate/restore) and a documented emergency process.

- Subprocessors: we need to provide the committed roster for private deploy infra only. I think standard subprocessors (cloud vendor for dedicated, monitoring vendor) are acceptable if scoped. Irene — can you pull the private-deploy subproc list and call out which ones touch telemetry?

- Network egress: procurement wants a binary classification column (customer payload | telemetry (opt-in/opt-out)). Update the spreadsheet and add a short description for each row.

- Breakglass: Acme requests attestation cadence. We typically offer quarterly audit summaries for private deployments and an evidence pack on request; for high-sensitivity customers we can agree to monthly attestation with fees. We should propose quarterly by default and allow a paid monthly cadence.

Can you please: (1) assemble a tracked-changes annex addressing the key bullets, (2) update the egress mapping spreadsheet with the requested columns, and (3) produce a short breakglass playbook stub (1-2 pages) that we can attach to the annex. A quick turnaround — can we have drafts back by 2026-05-07 12:00PM PT?

Thanks,
Jordan

--- Forwarded attachment: redlines-acme-dpa-20260505.docx (from Brett) ---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA annex: network egress mapping + CMK operator responsibilities — updated annex and playbook

Hi all — thanks for the clear notes, Brett. Attached are the updated items:

1) DPA_Annex_CMK_Operator_Responsibilities_v1.1.pdf — tracked changes reflect: explicit CMK nondisclosure language, a clause that prohibits Redwood from exporting customer CMKs or initiating escrow/escrow rotations without written customer authorization, and an operator access carve-out limited to documented emergency processes (breakglass) with customer opt-in telemetry.

2) acme-egress-map-20260504.xlsx — updated with the requested binary classification column ("Payload" vs "Telemetry"), a new "Telemetry Opt-In" column, and short descriptions for all egress endpoints.

3) breakglass-playbook-20260507.pdf (1.5 pages) — outlines the steps, approval gates, evidence collection, and attestation cadence. Proposed default: quarterly attestation included in Dedicated/Private SLAs; monthly attestation available as a paid add-on. The playbook requires customer confirmation of the emergency contact list and a signed affidavit before operator key actions are permitted.

Responses to specific asks:
- Subprocessors: See worksheet tab "Subprocessors_PrivateDeploy" in the egress map workbook. This is the committed roster for private deployments. Middleware monitoring vendor does capture anonymized telemetry by default; we included an opt-out switch that disables telemetry sinks at deployment time.
- Operator breakglass attestation cadence: proposed quarterly (included). Monthly attestation available for a fee; we included the language in the annex to reflect both options and the fee schedule.
- CMK export/escrow: explicit prohibition added; emergency procedure is documented and requires three-person approval (customer emergency contact + Redwood Security lead + legal approval).

Next steps: Brett / Acme Legal — please review the tracked annex and playbook. If acceptable, we can convert to final clean copy and route for signature. If you want alternate wording on the escrow/export paragraph, flag line 45-52 in the PDF.

Jordan — tagging for signature path once Acme confirms.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: DPA_Annex_CMK_Operator_Responsibilities_v1.1.pdf, acme-egress-map-20260504.xlsx, breakglass-playbook-20260507.pdf
